title: Porcine Circovirus in Denmark: Occurrence, Genetic Diversity and Phylogenetic Relationships
content: Porcine circovirus type 2 (PCV2) is an important virus due to its association with a range of clinical syndromes. PCV2 is classified into eight genotypes, PCV2a-PCV2h, of which PCV2a, PCV2b, and PCV2d are the major genotypes. Porcine circovirus type 3 (PCV3) is a more recently identified virus classified into two genotypes, PCV3a and PCV3b. To investigate the genetic diversity of PCV2 and PCV3 in Danish pigs, samples collected between 2014-2025 from herds without specific clinical signs associated with PCV2 or PCV3 were analyzed and sequenced. Phylogenetic analysis of 139 PCV2 strains showed that PCV2b was the dominant genotype until 2017, when PCV2d was first detected in Denmark. Since 2019, PCV2d has been the dominant genotype, while sporadic cases of PCV2a and PCV2b continue to occur. The occurrence of PCV3 was investigated in samples from 113 herds. PCV3 was detected in a high proportion of herds across all herd types, but there was no evidence that it caused specific clinical disease. Phylogenetic analysis of 21 PCV3 strains showed that all belonged to genotype PCV3a. This study provides insight into the long-term genetic diversity of PCV2 and PCV3 and serves as a basis for prevention and control of infections with these viruses.
